title: Open direct-image constructibility on arbitrary curves
statement:
Let $T$ be of finite type of dimension at most one over
a finite field or its algebraic closure, let
$j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be open, and let $A$ be finite
and killed by a power of a prime invertible on $T$.
For a constructible
etale $A$-module sheaf $F$, every
$R^qj_*F$ is
constructible on $T$.

proof.text: Write $k$ for the ground field and choose the prime $\ell$ and an integer $N\geq1$ with $\ell^N A=0$ as in the hypotheses. By [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], $T$ is locally Noetherian, since the spectrum of a field is locally Noetherian; finite type includes quasi-compactness by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], every open of $T$ is Noetherian. Thus $j$ is quasi-compact (intersect $U$ with any affine open of $T$) and quasi-separated (its diagonal is an isomorphism). These are the hypotheses needed for the stalk formula below. For $q<0$, the injective-resolution formula of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives zero: a sheaf placed in degree zero has an injective resolution in nonnegative degrees, so its termwise direct image has no negative cohomology. Degree zero is [thm-fin-open-degree-zero], and degrees $q>1$ vanish by [thm-exc-curve-open-dimension-general]; the zero sheaf is lisse. It remains to prove constructibility of $G=R^1j_*F$.

source.place: first paragraph: degree zero and degrees greater than one; hypotheses of the stalk formula

proof.text: Put $C=\overline U$ and $Z=C\setminus U$, both closed subsets of $T$. The closed subsets $C$ and $Z$ have finite irreducible decompositions by [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], and each component has a generic point by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Every generic point of a component $C_i$ of $C$ belongs to $U$: the nonempty open part of $C_i$ outside the other components meets $U$ by its density in $C$, and an open meeting an irreducible component contains its generic point. If an irreducible component $D$ of $Z$ were not a singleton, its generic point $d$ would have a proper specialization $e$. Then $\overline{\{e\}}\subsetneq D\subsetneq C_i$ for a component $C_i$ containing $D$, the second inclusion being strict because its generic point lies in $U$. This contradicts the dimension bound in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Thus $Z$ is a finite union of closed singletons, hence a finite set of closed points of $T$. This proves the boundary fact directly; it creates no node.

source.place: second paragraph: the boundary is a finite set of closed points

proof.text: The restriction $j^{-1}G$ is zero. Indeed, compute $Rj_*F$ by $j_*I^\bullet$ using [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; exactness of inverse image on constant-$A$ modules is [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The counit $j^{-1}j_*\to\mathrm{id}$ is a natural isomorphism on abelian sheaves by the first clause of [lem-kun-open-immersion-restriction]. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], the module inverse-image/direct-image adjunction has this same underlying counit. It therefore gives an $A$-linear isomorphism in each degree; naturality with respect to the differentials makes these a chain isomorphism $j^{-1}(j_*I^\bullet)\cong I^\bullet$. Its positive cohomology is zero, since $I^\bullet$ resolves $F$ in degree zero. On $W=T\setminus C$ the same representative restricts to zero termwise: every etale object over $W$ has empty fibre product with $U$, and the direct-image formula evaluates each $I^n$ on that empty object, giving zero. Restriction to $W$ is exact by the same inverse-image theorem. Consequently $G$ is zero on the open $V=T\setminus Z=U\amalg W$.

source.place: second paragraph: vanishing on U and outside its closure

proof.text: Fix $t\in Z$ and a geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ above it. Put $S=T_{(\bar t)}$. The coefficient-forgetting comparison [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] and the strict-local stalk formula [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] identify the underlying group of $G_{\bar t}$ with $H^1(U\times_T S,F_S)$, where $F_S$ is the underlying abelian pullback of $F$. The hypotheses of the latter formula hold: $j$ is qcqs by step 1, and the sheaf is torsion since $\ell^N A=0$.

source.place: Paragraph 1: strict-local stalk formula, Stacks Tag 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images).

proof.text: Choose an affine chart $i:\operatorname{Spec}D\hookrightarrow T$ containing $t$ with $D$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra, as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $\mathfrak p$ be its prime corresponding to $t$, and $K$ the separable closure of $\kappa(t)$ inside $\Omega$. Apply [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] to this chart and geometric point. It identifies $S$ over $T$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R$, where $R=(D_{\mathfrak p})^{\mathrm{sh}}$, and gives its strictly henselian local structure and residue field $K$. Under this identification the closed point maps to $t$ by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-closed-fiber-backward].

source.place: Paragraph 1: the geometric/algebraic strict-local comparison needed before the branch lemma; Stacks Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring).

proof.text: The point $t$ is closed by step 2, so [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a) gives that $\kappa(t)$ is finite over $k$. If $k$ is finite, then $\kappa(t)$ is finite and [lem-sfb-finite-field-separable-closure-algebraic] says that this very separable closure $K$ is an algebraic closure. If $k$ is algebraically closed, every element of the finite extension $\kappa(t)/k$ has a linear minimal polynomial, so $\kappa(t)=k$; the same argument in the algebraic extension $K/k$ gives $K=k$. Thus $K$ is algebraically closed in both cases, of positive characteristic $p=\operatorname{char}k$.

source.place: Paragraph 1: algebraically closed positive-characteristic residue field for the branch lemma; finite-field case is Stacks Tag 030Z (algebra-lemma-perfect).

proof.text: By [lem-exc-field-algebra-strict-henselization-excellent], both $R$ and $B=R/\sqrt{(0)}$ are excellent and Noetherian. Since $\sqrt{(0)}$ lies in the maximal ideal, [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-quotient] makes $B$ local and strictly henselian with residue field $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c), $D_{\mathfrak p}\cong\mathcal O_{T,t}$. Apply [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] to $T$ and [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension] to $D_{\mathfrak p}$ to obtain $\dim R=\dim\mathcal O_{T,t}\leq\dim T\leq1$. The ring $B$ is reduced: if a power of a class is nilpotent, its representative is nilpotent. Every prime of $R$ contains the nilradical, so taking inverse images along $R\to B$ identifies prime chains of $B$ with those of $R$, preserving strict inclusions. Hence $\dim B=\dim R\leq1$.

source.place: Paragraph 1: local-algebra hypotheses for the branch lemma; Stacks Tags 04MU (properties-lemma-dimension), 06LK (more-algebra-lemma-henselization-dimension), and the cited excellence and quotient interfaces.

proof.text: Put $V_R=U\times_T\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $P=V_R\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism], $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and its base change $P\to V_R$ are universal homeomorphisms. Therefore [prop-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-topos] identifies $H^1(V_R,F_S)$ with $H^1(P,F_P)$, with $F_P$ the pulled-back sheaf retaining its $A$-action. The closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ maps to the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, hence to $t\notin U$ by steps 5-7; thus $P$ misses it. If $\dim B=0$, every prime equals the maximal ideal and that ideal is zero because $B$ is reduced. Hence $B$ is a field and $P$ is empty, so the stalk is zero (the empty-cover sheaf axiom gives only the zero abelian sheaf and zero cohomology). Otherwise $\dim B=1$. The ring $B$ is reduced, excellent, local and strictly henselian with algebraically closed residue field of positive characteristic by steps 5-7, exactly the hypotheses of [lem-exc-punctured-curve-branches]. Its punctured spectrum is therefore a finite disjoint union $\coprod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Spec}K_i$, each $K_i$ the fraction field of an excellent strictly henselian DVR with that same residue field. Since $P$ is an open of this puncture and every field spectrum is a single point, $P=\coprod_{i\in I_U}\operatorname{Spec}K_i$ for a subset $I_U\subseteq I$, possibly empty. No density or irreducibility of $T$ is assumed.

source.place: first paragraph: reduction to branch fields; reduction invariance is Stacks Tag 03SI (etale-cohomology-proposition-topological-invariance).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct-cohomology-assembly], $H^1(P,F_P)=\prod_{i\in I_U}H^1(\operatorname{Spec}K_i,F_i)$ for the underlying abelian sheaves. Each $F_i$ has finite geometric fibre: [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies a pullback stalk with its original stalk, and [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-finite-stalks] gives finiteness of every original geometric fibre of the constructible $A$-module sheaf $F$. The exact, sections-compatible equivalence [lem-exc-field-discrete-modules] identifies $F_i$ with a finite discrete continuous $A[G_i]$-module $M_i$ and its section functor with invariants. An exact equivalence preserves injectives: transport a lifting problem across its exact inverse, solve it in the original injective, and transport the lift back. Applying this to injective resolutions identifies module-sheaf cohomology with the derived invariants defining continuous cohomology in [def-exc-continuous-cohomology]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget], its underlying group is the abelian cohomology occurring above. Since $\ell$ is invertible on $T$ it differs from $p$, the common residue characteristic of these branch DVRs. The finite-module clause of [lem-exc-dvr-galois] gives finiteness of each $H^1(G_i,M_i)$. Their finite product is finite, including the empty product. Steps 4-9 show that $G_{\bar t}$ is finite for every geometric point above every $t\in Z$.

source.place: first paragraph: finiteness of branch-field first cohomology and the stalk. Field/Galois comparison: Stacks Tags 03QT and 03QU (etale-cohomology.tex).

proof.text: Give each singleton $\{t\}\subseteq Z$ its reduced point-scheme structure $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$. The restriction of $G$ there has finite geometric fibre by step 9 and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. Put $G_t=\operatorname{Gal}(\kappa(t)^{\rm sep}/\kappa(t))$. Under [lem-exc-field-discrete-modules] the restriction is a finite continuous $A[G_t]$-module $M_t$. Intersect the finitely many open stabilizers of all elements of $M_t$ to obtain the open kernel $H$ of $G_t\to\operatorname{Aut}_A(M_t)$. As a kernel it is normal, and $G_t/H$ is finite because it embeds into the permutation group of the finite set $M_t$. Apply [lem-exc-etale-field-galois-classification] to the finite transitive continuous set $G_t/H$: it supplies a finite separable extension $L/\kappa(t)$ with stabilizer $H$ after choosing the embedding. Its spectrum is an etale cover by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale]. The geometric fibre over $L$ has the same underlying module with the action restricted to $H$, since a geometric automorphism over $L$ acts on the same fibre. Thus this cover trivializes the module sheaf by the field equivalence, so the restriction to the point is finite locally constant. Finally $V$ and these finitely many point schemes form a finite locally closed constructible partition: constructibility of these subsets follows from the Noetherian clause of [def-weil-constructible-subset]. On $V$, $G=0$ by step 3; on the point strata it is finite locally constant as just proved. The definition [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] gives constructibility of $G$, completing degree one and hence all degrees.

source.place: second paragraph: finite continuous Galois modules give lisse point strata and a finite constructible partition
